challengeFindings.title: A green affected-only `pull_request` CI run at the base sha settles verdict `none` (source `ci`) while the failing tests are red on `dev`

A gate red on a non-test stage (coverage threshold, a static check after the unit run) plus base-red test cases reads `all`, so the pause tells the owner "no round here can fix them" while the branch's own failure keeps the gate red after `dev` is fixed

A base file run that crashes (non-zero exit, report written without the failing case, e.g. a load error in the fresh checkout) counts the case `absent`, so the verdict reads `none` and the pause says "the failures come from this branch"

`withoutHooks` wraps the whole base run, so `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` / `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` leaks into the install and every base test process; a test that drives git hooks fails at base only and reads `red`, turning a branch-caused failure into `all`
Two base cases with the same name in one file (an `it.each` with a repeated title) match by `find`, so a passing first twin hides a red second one and the case reads `pass`

A `Gate: FAIL` line smuggled into a pause item's text makes a resume close a non-gate pause (a challenge or verify-gap pause with hard blockers) as "Re-run gate" and continue without the owner's answer

challengeFindings.title: A failing case that is skipped at the base commit (an `it.skipIf` on an env var or a gitignored artefact the fresh checkout lacks) reads `pass`, so the verdict is `none` and the pause says "the failures come from this branch" with no evidence either way

With one case red at base and the rest undetermined (their base file run crashed, or no file resolved), the verdict is `some` with reason null, so the pause says "a round can fix 4 of 5" for 4 cases nothing is known about, and the crash reason that Task 17 added is dropped

A file holding two cases with the same name (an `it.each` title without a placeholder, or the same title in two `describe` blocks a runner does not prefix) matches the first one at base, so a case that fails at base reads `pass` (verdict `none`), or a case that passes at base reads `red` (a false `all` that recommends `Stop` and tells the owner to fix a healthy `dev`)

A `worktreeCopy` entry that `fs.cpSync` cannot copy (a FIFO or socket at `.env`, an unreadable file) throws out of `baseRun`, so `tests base` exits non-zero and the build takes the Failure Path instead of pausing with verdict `unknown`, breaking the verb's "exit 0 for every verdict" contract

A branch that breaks a shared setup file makes every test file fail, and `tests base` then re-runs every one of them at the base commit, one process at a time with no file cap and no timeout, so the Decision Pause waits for a serial re-run of the whole suite (or forever on a test that hangs in the fresh checkout)

The owner stops at a red-gate verify pause that also holds hard-blocker gaps (`test-loosened`, `exception-refused`, `no-test-first`), fixes `dev` and resumes; the resume writes `Decision: Re-run gate` under Q1 (with no loop question, that is the first hard blocker itself), sets `Status: DECIDED`, forces `VERIFY_VERDICT` = PASS, and a green re-run builds the next group with every gap unanswered
